hotspots.title: Lecture hall
hotspots.text: You sit in your first programming class. The lecturer shows how a big problem is broken into small steps a computer can follow, one at a time.
hotspots.fact: Programming starts with logic, not with typing code.

hotspots.title: Coding lab
hotspots.text: You write a short program, run it, and it fails. You read the error, change one line, and try again until it works.
hotspots.fact: Finding and fixing mistakes is a big part of the daily work.

hotspots.title: Server room
hotspots.text: Racks of machines hum and blink. Here you learn how data travels across networks and how systems are kept safe and running.
hotspots.fact: Most people only notice this layer when it breaks.

hotspots.title: Project studio
hotspots.text: A small team plans an app on a board full of tasks. You split the work, share progress, and fit your parts together.
hotspots.fact: Working well in a team matters as much as technical skill.

hotspots.title: Tech office
hotspots.text: You join a company as an intern. You help test a new feature, join a stand-up meeting, and see how your classes connect to real products.
hotspots.fact: Careers range from building software to securing systems and analyzing data.
